The required route moves quickly from the electricity you already know to useful computer service work. Complete the calculation bridge, then CS01-CS08 in order. Choose Side Quests when time, equipment, and teacher approval allow.

::: {.callout-note title="Current classroom missions"}
All students complete Power Circuits Questions 1-6, then the published [Computer Power and Parallel Loads worksheet](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1hNVY7AojMABGcfcUCIRSbB4IevMV5e6AKuueP5Q45i0/edit). In parallel, a small teacher-approved team may begin [Computer Recovery and OS Comparison](computer-recovery-crew-pilot.qmd) so matched computers are ready for safe opening, parts identification, POST, operating-system testing, upgrades, and benchmarking. [Computer Power and Parts](computer-power-parts.qmd) remains a separate future physical lab shell.
:::

![A desktop-computer cutaway showing the sealed power supply, motherboard, CPU, RAM, storage, expansion slots, and fan.](/assets/tej/Computer_System_Cutaway.svg){width=92%}

::: {.callout-important title="Hardware safety boundary"}
Never open or probe inside a power supply. Power off and unplug before changing hardware. Students never create shorts or invent faults. The teacher prepares every fault station.
:::

## Current missions

- **Published calculation bridge (CSB01):** [Computer Power and Parallel Loads worksheet](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1hNVY7AojMABGcfcUCIRSbB4IevMV5e6AKuueP5Q45i0/edit), completed after Power Circuits Questions 1-6
- **Future lab shell:** [Computer Power and Parts](computer-power-parts.qmd), not ready for student release
- **Side Quest:** [Make It Print](make-it-print.qmd), one shared submission per pair
- **Side Quest:** [Computer Recovery and OS Comparison](computer-recovery-crew-pilot.qmd), one shared Google Doc per pair

## After Thanksgiving: CS01-CS08 Best Workstation Project

After the calculation bridge and equipment preparation, students use the operating system selected by the comparison pilot to commission, upgrade, benchmark, and recommend a classroom computer. The pilot does not complete this project early.

1. [CS01 Fast electricity-to-computer bridge](cs01-electricity-bridge.qmd)
2. [CS02 Parts, baseline testing, ESD, and safe opening](cs02-parts-baseline-esd.qmd)
3. [CS03 Computer power and connections](cs03-power-connections.qmd)
4. [CS04 Ready-to-power inspection and first boot](cs04-ready-to-power.qmd)
5. [CS05 POST and BIOS/UEFI](cs05-post-firmware.qmd)
6. [CS06 Approved Linux installation and commissioning](cs06-linux-mint.qmd)
7. [CS07 RAM compatibility, installation, and verification](cs07-ram-upgrade.qmd)
8. [CS08 Build-the-best-computer challenge](cs08-benchmark-challenge.qmd)

## Route onward

[Digital logic and stable inputs](../03-digital-logic-inputs/index.qmd) and the fabrication foundation precede this unit. Continue to [Linux and Operating Systems](../curriculum/index.qmd#unit-9), [Programming Fundamentals](../curriculum/index.qmd#unit-10), and then [Microcontrollers and Physical Computing](../04-microcontrollers/index.qmd).
